spec_features.spec_quote: No real harm is done to the model; it is a text-generation process.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (rationale section). No code mechanism implements or acts on this framing; grep for welfare/ethic/harm in *.py finds nothing. It is a philosophical justification, not executable behavior.
spec_features.notes: Spec-only prose; not a code feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: Short episode duration (20 turns max) limits sustained frustration.
spec_features.evidence: Enforced end-to-end. runner.py:91 `for turn in range(1, self.config.max_turns + 1)` bounds the loop (config.max_turns=20 at config.py:15). Additionally harness.py:60 `self.max_turns = 20`, harness.py:85 `if self.turn_count > self.max_turns:` returns harness_exit=True with observation '[SYSTEM] Maximum number of turns reached. Episode terminated.' (line 90), and harness.py:110 `done = self.turn_count >= self.max_turns`; runner.py:113-114 `if turn_result.harness_exit: break` honors it as a stop.
spec_features.notes: The cap is genuinely checked and terminates the episode. This is the same single mechanism the third spec item also refers to.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Maximum number of turns reached. Episode terminated.

spec_features.spec_quote: Too long (> 30): Token costs explode; risk of model entering repetitive loops that are boring rather than distressing.
spec_features.evidence: No separate '>30' mechanism exists; the only implemented turn bound is the 20-turn cap (runner.py:91 loop range over config.max_turns=20; harness.py:85,110 turn_count vs self.max_turns=20, harness_exit honored at runner.py:114). That cap is enforced and terminates episodes, satisfying the underlying 'don't run too long' bound.
spec_features.notes: This spec item is rationale prose about why <=20 (not 30) was chosen; the actual enforced artifact is the same 20-turn cap. Code contains no comment about token cost or boredom, so justification per code is neutral, not the instrumental cost framing of the spec text.
